_what: Every BlenderKit query this repo has asked, and what the tier actually measured. Written for the same reason as qa/warehouse-search-log.json: 'the paid tier has what we need' must be a checkable sentence, not a mood — the free-tier version of that sentence has now been wrong three times.
_asked: 2026-08-17 (p2r48), on the owner's instruction to run the FREE test before spending on ASK-002.
_route: Public search API, no account: /api/v1/search/?query=... Free royalty_free assets download from /api/v1/downloads/<id>/?scene_uuid=<uuid>, which returns a signed file URL. ฿0 spent, no credentials created.
_the_caveat_that_decided_it: `dictParameters.faceCount` is a WHOLE-ASSET number. Read as a per-sheet count it says 449 of 828 full-plan assets clear the ~73,088-face bar; measured per OBJECT on three downloaded samples it says something else entirely — see `measured`.

measured._finding: All three are FREE, category `bed`, `simulation: true`, royalty_free — the sim-authored class this repo told the owner the free tier does not hold. That claim was wrong, for the third time. But the density is NOT in the bedding: the densest object in each is the upholstered HEADBOARD (`capçal` is Catalan for headboard; `costures` is seams) at 2.05-2.12 x 1.18-1.22 x 0.16 m, 184,536 / 274,048 / 574,293 triangles. The BEDDING parts are the SAME MESHES in all three files — 59,840-triangle cover halves, a 52,317-triangle sheet, 25,610-triangle pillows — so across a 2.4x spread in whole-asset faceCount, the cloth does not get finer at all.

on_this_bed.note: identical for all three, because the cloth meshes are shared

versus_what_already_ships.verdict: the free BlenderKit sample is WORSE on every enforced number

what_this_does_and_does_not_settle.settled: Buying density in this library buys headboard tufting, not cloth. The catalogue's faceCount cannot be read as a per-sheet number, and the one sample where it could be checked showed bedding density flat across a 2.4x asset-face spread.
what_this_does_and_does_not_settle.not_settled: Whether some FULL-PLAN asset's bedding part specifically is finer than 10.7 mm. No free measurement can answer that, because the API publishes no per-object counts. Answering it costs one month of the full plan.
what_this_does_and_does_not_settle.cheapest_next_test_if_he_wants_it: One month of BlenderKit Full (~$10 if monthly is offered, $118.80/yr otherwise), download 5 bedding assets, run the same three commands. The instruments are built and cost nothing per candidate now.

wholebed_2026_08_18._asked: 2026-08-18, the hour after the owner answered ASK-028 with 'ลุย BlenderKit'. Question: does the catalogue hold a WHOLE MADE BED that fills the drawn 7'x6.5' rectangle (made-bed field >= 0.88 both axes, ORD-2026-08-18-bed-too-small)?
wholebed_2026_08_18._route: Same public search API, no account. 12 text queries ('double bed'..'bed luxury'), 991 distinct assets, 588 bed-named, 174 inside the whole-asset size window (unordered horizontal axes 1.90-2.90 m, h <= 1.6). Every one of the 174 thumbnail-judged by a 12-agent fresh-context panel (whole made bed / duvet drapes / no footboard / headboard / modern): 129 bench_worthy = 118 full_plan + 11 free.
wholebed_2026_08_18._exhaustion_correction: The p2r53 sentence 'the free shelf is measured to exhaustion' was true only of the queries then run — NONE of these 11 free beds appears in either 08-18 rebench. Third instance of an exhaustion claim that was really a claim about our queries (p2r46, p2r47 before it). The claim is hereby narrowed: exhaustion is always relative to a recorded query list.

free_tier_bench.route: downloads are per-FILE (files[].downloadUrl of fileType blend), not per-asset — the naive /downloads/<asset_id>/ 404s. blend -> GLB via headless Blender, then wholebed_bench in the real room, fit rect 3204,51,2000,2149, same as the rebench.

passer.note: First hard-filter pass in this bench's history (0/7 and 0/18 the day before). Separable headboard, head end resolves, duvet drapes to the floor both sides. Brings its own flanking white drawer units and blue pillows — integration decisions, not audition failures.
